title: staging add: lazy create from main, merge feature, staged-set store, build hook
action: New verb group `bee staging` with subcommand `add --feature <slug>` per staging-lane D0/D0a. Store .bee/runtime/staging.json on main: {branch:'staging', worktree_root, created_at, base_sha, staged:[{feature, branch, last_merged_sha, at}]} — CLI-only writes, atomic write pattern like existing runtime stores. Behavior: refuse outside the main checkout (reuse the ordinary-checkout check); lazily create branch 'staging' FROM CURRENT MAIN ONLY plus a worktree directory (sibling naming like bee worktree new: <repo>--wt--staging) when no staging record exists; merge the feature's branch (resolve via lane/worktree records like worktree merge does) into staging with --no-ff; on conflict: git merge --abort, typed STAGING_MERGE_CONFLICT naming feature+files, staged set unchanged; on success: upsert the feature into staged[], run config commands.staging_build when present (visible skip note when absent, never an error). Re-running add for the same feature re-merges (git picks up only new commits) and updates last_merged_sha. Register the verb in the dispatcher and registry_payload.json (hand-edit; no generator — keep tests/registry_contracts.rs green). Tests: scratch-repo fixture — lazy creation from main only; add merges and records; re-add after new commit fast-forwards content; conflict aborts clean with staging still usable; build cmd invoked when configured, skipped visibly when not.

truths: staging branch+worktree lazily created from main, never from a feature branch
add merges the feature branch and records it in staging.json
